create.name: Tsechen Namdrol Ling
create.bio:
Tsechen Namdrol Ling is a small Tibetan Buddhist centre of the Sakya school in northern New Mexico. Its name, which it renders as a place of complete liberation and great compassion, was given by Sakya Trichen Rinpoche, the 41st throne-holder of the Sakya school, who opened the centre in person in May 2014; it became a registered nonprofit in New Mexico the following year and continues under his guidance. After years of meeting in and around Santa Fe, the community acquired a permanent site in Jemez Springs.

Rather than keeping a resident teacher, the centre invites lamas and scholars to teach. Visitors have included Do Tulku Rinpoche, Glenn Mullin, Lama Jampa Thaye, Khenpo Migmar Tseten, Lama Choedak Rinpoche and Lama Kunga Thartse Rinpoche, and recordings of several of these teachings, on karma, shamatha meditation, mahamudra and the bardo, are shared on its YouTube channel. Its website gathers news of Sakya events, an online library of teachings by the lineage's heads, and ways to support the retreat land.

free_resources.description: The centre's page of online teachings from the Sakya lineage, including Sakya Trichen Rinpoche on the four seals and the basics of the Sakya path, with downloadable teaching texts and an interview with Jetsun Kushok Chimey Luding.

flags: Brand inbox: santa.fe_sakya@yahoo.com is the centre's general address (mailto link on the about and home pages).

Photo: no picture of a hall or building on the site. Used the channel avatar (an endless-knot emblem) and the site's own icon (a bronze of Virupa, the Sakya forefather); neither is a confirmed logo, so owner may want to check.

Thin centre: no regular classes or paid programmes of its own are published; items are its recorded teachings plus one resource page. Last full-length upload Feb 2026; about 3 evergreen uploads in the last 2 years (borderline on the channel rule).
Base: the about page says the centre now has a permanent location in Jemez Springs, New Mexico (a village of under 5,000 people); its earlier events were in Santa Fe.
Regional: northern New Mexico has few or no Spiritpedia listings.
Teachers file links lama-migmar-tseten as instructor: the about page lists Khenpo Migmar Tseten among the teachers the centre has hosted, and his talk 'The Play of Mahamudra' is on its channel.
Possible future listings: Do Tulku Rinpoche, Lama Jampa Thaye, Glenn Mullin, Lama Choedak Rinpoche (names only).
left_out: Lama Choedak Rinpoche's talk 'Understanding Anxiety and Depression' left out under the health rule.
Short clips (offering ceremonies, enthronement prayer, accessibility appeal, new works reel) left out as not teaching.
Events on the Coming Up page are run by other organisations (Bodhgaya empowerments, Ewam Choden Zoom meditations) and were not listed as the centre's offerings.
